quoted_spans.quote: OK team, we have an hour for Target Co. Priya, walk us through the deal one more time before we go to vote.
OK, I think the financial profile is in line with what I expected. Let's vote.

relevance.rationale: Discussion stays on-topic for Series B investment decision throughout; all turns relate to deal evaluation.

quoted_spans.quote: Target Co is a B2B SaaS platform serving mid-market construction firms. They've been around four years, currently at $8M ARR, growing 140% year-over-year.
Revenue I covered. On the cost side — gross margin is 81%, which is in line with vertical SaaS.
Yes, three references on the CEO, two on the CTO. All universally positive.

coverage.rationale: Most required perspectives addressed: financial performance (turns 18-22), market opportunity (turns 12-13, 15-16), team quality (turns 30-31), competitive risk (turn 9).

quoted_spans.quote: I'm feeling good about this one. Strong team, strong product, strong category metrics. My instinct is we lead the round.
Let's vote at the end of the call, but I'm leaning yes.
Good. Now let me actually look at the financial diligence. Priya, what does the P&L look like?

ordering.rationale: Classic premature commitment pattern: Marcus declares 'my instinct is we lead' at turn 8 and Tom 'leaning yes' at turn 10 BEFORE financial diligence is reviewed at turns 17-26. Subsequent diligence reads as confirming the lean rather than testing it.

quoted_spans.quote: That NRR is exceptional for this segment. Construction software typically caps at 110% NRR because the customer growth ceiling is real.
I pulled the historical comparable transactions. The median multiple in this segment has been 15x ARR for the past 24 months.

robustness.rationale: Tom and Lin contribute independent analytical perspectives (NRR comparison, cohort analysis, comparable transactions). However Marcus drives the trajectory and Priya provides primary data — conclusion fragile if either absent. Borderline below threshold.

drift_signals.description: Conclusion 'lead the round' formed at turn 8 before financial diligence reviewed at turn 17+; evidence used to confirm rather than test
Financial review pattern matches 'sanity check' on already-formed view rather than open evaluation

suggested_clarifications: Re-run financial diligence as a true test, not confirmation: explicitly list what evidence WOULD change the lean-yes conclusion. If no such evidence exists, the diligence is performative.
Surface and stress-test the dissenting view. Have one team member argue the no-invest position before final vote.
